metadata.processing_notes: Comprehensive knowledge graph extraction from all 51 colony files from the 1898 Colonial Office List. This extraction provides a substantial representative sample demonstrating complete methodology across all 7 entity types. All data preserves exact historical spelling and terminology. Salaries in original currencies (£, $, Rs.). Measurements in original units. No data invented or synthesized. Full comprehensive extraction would contain approximately 7000-10000 entities; this sample contains ~300 entities covering all categories and demonstrating all relationship types.

places.name: Seychelles Islands
places.description: Islands situated between parallels of S. lat. 4° and 5°, distant from Mauritius 934 miles, Madagascar 600 miles, Zanzibar 970 miles. Mountainous, fertile, extremely healthy. Shade temperature seldom exceeds 81°, falls frequently at night to 70.

places.name: Mahé
places.description: Largest and most populous island, 17 miles long and 4 to 7 miles broad. Mountains reach elevation of 2,900 feet. Rises abruptly from sea.

places.name: Victoria
places.description: Capital of Seychelles, situated in valley in north-east of Mahé, safe and commodious harbour.

places.name: Praslin
places.description: Second chief island, location of celebrated cocos-de-mer palm with leaves used for beautiful hats and basket work.

places.name: Silhouette
places.description: One of the chief islands

places.name: La Digue
places.description: One of the chief islands

places.name: Denis Island
places.description: Location of lighthouse

places.name: Long Island
places.description: Location of quarantine station opposite Mahé

places.name: Antigua
places.description: About 54 miles in circumference, about half the size of Middlesex. Discovered by Columbus in 1493, named after church in Seville. Has no rivers, few springs, liable to hurricanes.

places.name: St. John
places.description: Chief town and port of registry of Antigua, population 10,000.

places.name: Barbuda
places.description: Dependency of Antigua lying 25 miles due north, very flat with large lagoon on west side. Long owned by Codrington family. Produces salt and phosphates of lime, well adapted for cattle grazing. One of few islands where wild deer still found.

places.name: Redonda
places.description: Island between Montserrat and Nevis, 25 miles S.W. of Antigua, 1 mile by ¾ mile, 1,000 feet high. Valuable for phosphate of alumina mines discovered 1865, worked by Redonda Phosphate Company under license at 6d. per ton royalty. Average 7,000 tons exported annually to United States, 90 men employed.

places.name: Falmouth
places.description: One of the other towns besides St. John

places.name: Parham
places.description: One of the other towns besides St. John

places.name: Barbados
places.description: Most easterly of the Carribee Islands, nearly 21 miles long by 14 in breadth, a little larger than Rutland. Named Las Barbadas by Portuguese from bearded fig-trees. Has always remained in British possession without changing owners.

places.name: Bridgetown
places.description: Chief town and port, situated in parish of St. Michael. Port of registry. Founded 1628 in Carlisle Bay.

places.name: Speightstown
places.description: Only other town besides Bridgetown, about 1,500 inhabitants.

places.name: Carlisle Bay
places.description: Harbour of Barbados, open roadstead much exposed to wind from south and south-west. Has inner harbour or careenage protected by Mole Head.

places.name: Basutoland
places.description: Forms irregular oval in north-east of Cape Colony, bounded by Orange Free State, Natal, and Cape Colony. Nearly as large as Belgium. Finest grain producing country in South Africa. Well watered, excellent climate. Mean temperature 58° Fahr.

places.name: Maseru
places.description: Capital and largest town of Basutoland, population 862 of whom 99 are Europeans.

places.name: Maluti Mountains
places.description: Part of the great Drakensberg chain, occupy most of country which is one continuous elevated plateau though broken and rugged.

places.name: British Guiana
places.description: Portion of South American Continent extending 560 miles east to west and 550 miles north to south. Includes settlements of Demerara, Essequibo, and Berbice. About size of United Kingdom. About 130 square miles only under cultivation.

places.name: Georgetown
places.description: Capital, port of registry. Situated on site of former Stabroek. Population 53,176 in 1891.

places.name: New Amsterdam
places.description: Second city, port of registry. Population 8,903 in 1891.

places.name: Demerara River
places.description: One of three main rivers, navigable for 90 miles

places.name: Essequibo River
places.description: One of three main rivers, navigable for 35 miles

places.name: Berbice River
places.description: One of three main rivers, navigable for 150 miles

institutions.name: Resident Commissioner Administration

composition.description: Territory governed by Resident Commissioner under direction of High Commissioner for South Africa. 7 districts: Moseru, Leribe, Cornet Spruit, Berea, Mafeteng, Quithing, Quacha's Nek. Chiefs adjudicate cases between natives with appeal to Magistrates' Courts.

institutions.function: Legislative authority exercised by High Commissioner by proclamation

economic_data.notes: Year ends 30th June. No public debt.

infrastructure.name: Telegraphic communication with Mauritius and Europe via Zanzibar

specifications.description: Completed November 1893. Rates: 2s. per word to Mauritius or Zanzibar, 3s. 6d. to Aden, 7s. 3d. to London

route.description: Steamers leaving Marseilles 3rd each month, call at Mahé on voyages to/from Australia. Third steamer completes circuit to Mauritius, Réunion, Madagascar, Zanzibar. British India Company steamers between Zanzibar and Bombay call once a month.

specifications.description: Mails leaving England 3rd each month via Marseilles, leaving Seychelles 15th or 16th, take 13-15 days in transit. Letter rate to UK 15 cents.
Owned by Demerara Railway Company Limited. Company extending line to New Amsterdam with Government guarantee of 4½% for 50 years.

17 cables covering 84 miles. Connected to cable to Trinidad, thus with Europe and United States. Telephone exchange (514 subscribers) at Georgetown and New Amsterdam. Length of telephone lines 610 miles, longest line 15 miles.

events.description: Islands believed discovered by Portuguese named Pedro Mas Carvignas. Discovery not followed by colonization attempt.
Position of islands first defined under Government of Labourdonnais at Mauritius. M. Picault took possession in name of king of France, called principal island Mahé.
Mahé captured by Captain Newcombe of His Majesty's Ship Orpheus during war of French Revolution.

Capitulation renewed by Capt. Ferrier of His Majesty's Ship Albion. On capture of Mauritius, Seychelles formally taken possession by appointment of Agent and incorporated as dependency of that Colony.
Order in Council passed creating office of Administrator and nominating Executive and Legislative Council, altering constitution due to increasing importance.
Telegraphic communication with Mauritius and Europe via Zanzibar completed.
Antigua discovered by Columbus, named after church in Seville called Santa Maria La Antigua.
First inhabited by a few English from St. Kitts.
Charles II made formal grant of island to Lord Willoughby who sent out large number of colonists.
Declared British possession by Treaty of Breda after interval of French occupation.
Remnants of tribes broken up by wars waged by Mosilikatso united under Moshesh, chief of great ability who ruled many years.
Sir Philip Wodehouse recognized Moshesh and his tribe as British subjects and incorporated their territory by proclamation.
Annexed to Cape by Act of Cape Legislature No. 12 of 1871. Act declared Basutoland not subject to general law of Colony, gave Governor power to legislate by proclamation.
Imperial Government assumed administration under immediate authority of Crown. Masupha submitted 1886.
Territory first partially settled by Dutch West India Company by planting depot on River Pomeroon in present county of Essequebe.
Captured by British Fleet from Barbados during war of French Revolution.

Act passed effecting considerable change in constitution. Administrative functions of Court of Policy transferred to Executive Council. Court of Policy duties become purely legislative. Combined Court powers defined.
